segments.english: You have shown to know why the Ribash did not stumble in it it is due to that he did not receive it from mouth to mouth , not due to any prompting as you say And here are the words of the second witness, the Gaon, the author of Chavot Yair, of blessed memory in very great brevity who was asked by a certain sage who spent his days in the Gemara and the decisors and behold a spirit rose within him and stirred him to study the Kabbalah for the excellence of its virtues, which is the soul of the Torah and he saw how many sayings of the Zohar that it is impossible to enter before the Holy King except by it and the sages of the Talmud did not command about it only warned that not to expound it what is beyond you, do not seek, etc. and he asked the Rabbi to free him from confusion and he answered and said to him Woe is me if I advise you about withdrawal and cause slackening of hands and hindrance from this wisdom this, which is without doubt the soul of the Torah and the root of faith, like wisdom and knowledge and understanding and without doubt, that he merited it he is of the sons of the height; happy is he how good is his portion and how pleasant is his greatness beloved on high, etc. He cited the words of Yish'ar of Candia who went at very great length and gathered like sheaves on the threshing floor the majority of opinions that preceded him to bring near, and not to distance against the book Bechinat ha-Dat, which sought to lead many astray! And he said that he found a peg fixed in a pillar of iron, in a faithful place to hang on to it to agree to receive a reward for withdrawal more than inquiry in the book Shemen la-Ma'or, of the father of the Rav and these are his words, briefly: " And this thing that he wrote in the name of Rabbi Meir Gabbai that everyone who has not received the secrets of the Torah from his master and thinks to weigh them in his mind transgresses the prohibition 'you shall not make for yourself a graven image' I said in my heart to rouse the ways of people in our generation I have seen infants who have not seen light, who say 'my mothers, I have seen light' hidden within them, like the leaven of chicks that their eyes were not enticed, etc. and even the great ones who are in the land whoever is sharp and diligent, expert in the chambers of Torah. has no strength in his intellect to grasp the chambers of light but only from the mouth of an elder and teacher." and these are his words: the Ramban in his introduction to the commentary on the Torah: " And I bring a faithful covenant and it gives proper counsel to everyone who looks into this book that he should not suppose a supposition and not think thoughts about the matter of all the hints that I write in the secrets of the Torah, for I inform faithfully that my words are not grasped by any reason or understanding except from the mouth of a wise, received sage, to balance, receiving, understanding And the reasoning in them is folly of great harm, preventing benefit, etc." If you say that I am explaining the Ramban that all his words are briefly by allusion, unlike other books of Kabbalah that explained their words. Do you not see in Sha'arei Orah that he wrote on every page the phrase 'I hereby allude.' So too, in the book of Rabbeinu Bachya, he made it very brief and was accustomed to say in his own words "and the wise will understand," all the more so the book of the Zohar, which is sealed and locked and these are his words, Etz Chayyim in his introduction: " Although it is certain that in the later generations they are sustained from this composition. There is no doubt that the waters of wisdom will not be revealed to every man by the power of contemplation according to their human intellect but only through a flow of divine influence that flows upon him." And if the last of the Kabbalists went so far as to say that his words are not grasped, how can it arise in the mind that human reason, especially among the people of our generation, this to understand and comprehend the words of the living God Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, whose voice of his words is flames of fire and they are sealed with a thousand locks, etc. Therefore, men of heart, hear me and do not destroy yourselves by looking into later books built according to their human intellect, see there And in my opinion, that when a man sins in the reflection of the thought in the World of Emanation, his iniquity is unbearable. Although many, and also perfect ones, of the later Kabbalists aroused the hearts of people greatly to study the Kabbalah and wrote that the one who withholds himself from studying Kabbalah is pushed away from its precinct and loses his world. It seems to me that they do not disagree, and surely whoever can learn from the mouth of a divine Kabbalist who will explain to him the matters as the Ari did for his disciples happy is his portion. Even though the later ones permitted study from the books and understanding from one's own mind "better is the fingernail of the early ones, etc." Sit and do not do is better, since the danger of the body is greater, all the more so the soul, etc." And we may not inquire into hidden things but only to hear in the study of the plain meaning of Scripture and the rebuke of morality, to walk in the ways of the upright for our knowledge is short. Thus far the words of Shemen la-Ma'or, from which the proof from him is to agree to withdrawal, etc. And with all this I have made known to you my opinion and do not rely on me, neither you nor another for I am not fit to decide And here I liken the study of this holy of holies to a journey to the land of holiness for its virtue is known, as they said in the Talmud "that without it is like one who has no God and one who worships idols, and one who walks four cubits in Eretz Israel is a son of the World to Come, and many praises." And even so, the Tosafot wrote in the name of Rabbi Chayyim that now it is not a commandment to dwell in the land. for there are many commandments dependent on the land which we are not able to fulfil on them And also because of the danger of the roads, and because of the poverty there, which will make him transgress against his opinion and against the opinion of his Maker there. And if there is no expert before him and a guard superior against all harms, it is good to refrain from this! Surely also who will deny the virtue of this wisdom, exalted above without measure. on condition that one merits it, to learn it from the mouth of a Kabbalist who also received it from his master. And indeed it is true that I am astonished at books composed by later authors that brought sayings of the Zohar. and they raise difficulties about them and explain them according to their own judgment. Who gave permission to human reason to invent by his own judgment the existence of the first three and three purities? For it is explained in the Zohar that there is a place where no question arises about it, etc. and there is no proof from the saying of the Zohar and Sefer Yetzirah and Rabbi Meir, who received from the mouth of the Elder of Elders and Elijah and the supernal holy ones supernal, and all those children of the Zohar, the spirit of the LORD spoke in them and His word was on their tongue. And also the Ari and his disciples, who received from him mouth to mouth from the mouth of the supernal ones, the words came forth and we, in our study of those, it does not occur to our mind except the reading of the words what is not so with these later ones and those who explain from their own judgment.

grammar: The paragraph is one long period built on the Hebrew conjunction ו, with the author's own words, the letter of Chavot Yair, and a series of quotations (Shemen ha-Ma'or quoting R. Meir Gabbai, the Ramban's introduction, Etz Chayyim's introduction) set inside it; the quotation formulas (וז"ל, ע"כ) mark where each begins and ends.
The verb הראית is a perfect addressed to the reader, with the infinitive לדעת after it: 'you have shown [us] to know why'.
ע"כ in the middle of the paragraph (token 523) closes the quotation from Shemen ha-Ma'or, and the translation gives it as 'Thus far'.
The Hebrew uses many quotations of the Talmud and the Zohar without a reference; no reference is added (decisions, Quotations section).

Quotations without a source reference are given as the author gives them; the Bible verse Deut 6:13 is not quoted here.
context: The Ribash is Rabbi Yitzchak ben Sheshet; Yish'ar of Candia, Ramban, Chavot Yair and Rabbeinu Bachya are the authorities the author cites.
